chapters.title: Forms
chapters.subtitle: forms.py, ModelForm, validation, widgets, formsets and files
chapters.summary: The complete forms.py working guide: a plain form end to end, the validation pipeline, ModelForm saves, widgets, formsets, files, and the exact fixes for the errors that stop a beginner.
chapters.quick_answer: A form is a validation and rendering layer. Define fields in `forms.py`, bind it with `request.POST` and `request.FILES`, call `is_valid()`, then use `cleaned_data`. Use `ModelForm` when the shape matches a model; use a plain `Form` for everything else.

sections.title: The 30-second answer
sections.body:
A **bound** form has data (`Form(request.POST)`); an **unbound** form does not (`Form()`). `is_valid()` runs validation and returns a boolean. `cleaned_data` exists only after validation succeeds. `form.errors` is a dictionary of lists of messages.

A form does not save anything by itself. You decide what happens after `is_valid()`: send an email, create an object, redirect. `ModelForm.save()` is a convenience, not magic.

sections.title: A plain Form, end to end
sections.body:
Start with `forms.Form`, one field per input. Field arguments handle the common rules: `required`, `max_length`, `min_length`, `choices`, `initial`, `help_text`, `label`. Widgets control the HTML, not the validation.

In the view, use the POST/redirect/GET pattern: validate on POST, redirect on success, and render the bound form with errors on failure.
sections.code:
# forms.py
from django import forms

class ContactForm(forms.Form):
    name = forms.CharField(max_length=80, label="Your name")
    email = forms.EmailField(label="Email address")
    topic = forms.ChoiceField(
        choices=[
            ("support", "Support"),
            ("billing", "Billing"),
            ("other", "Something else"),
        ]
    )
    message = forms.CharField(
        widget=forms.Textarea(attrs={"rows": 6, "placeholder": "How can we help?"}),
        min_length=20,
        max_length=4000,
    )
    consent = forms.BooleanField(label="I agree to be contacted")

# views.py
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from .forms import ContactForm

def contact(request):
    form = ContactForm(request.POST or None)
    if request.method == "POST" and form.is_valid():
        # cleaned_data is typed and validated
        send_contact_email(
            name=form.cleaned_data["name"],
            email=form.cleaned_data["email"],
            topic=form.cleaned_data["topic"],
            message=form.cleaned_data["message"],
        )
        return redirect("pages:contact_success")
    return render(request, "pages/contact.html", {"form": form})
sections.note: `request.POST or None` keeps the form unbound on GET. Passing an empty QueryDict would make it bound and immediately invalid.

sections.title: Fields and widgets at a glance
sections.body:
A field validates and converts. A widget renders. Most form work is choosing the right pair.

- `CharField` → `TextInput` (short text)
- `EmailField` → `EmailInput` (email validation included)
- `SlugField` → `TextInput` (URL-safe text)
- `IntegerField`, `DecimalField` → `NumberInput`
- `BooleanField` → `CheckboxInput`
- `DateField`, `DateTimeField` → `DateInput`, `DateTimeInput`
- `ChoiceField` → `Select` or `RadioSelect`
- `ModelChoiceField` → `Select` populated from a queryset
- `FileField`, `ImageField` → `FileInput` (needs `request.FILES`)

Pass `widget=forms.Textarea(attrs={"rows": 8})` when the default widget is wrong. Use `forms.HiddenInput` for values the user should not edit, but never trust a hidden field for authorization.
sections.code:
class ProfileForm(forms.Form):
    display_name = forms.CharField(max_length=80)
    email = forms.EmailField(widget=forms.EmailInput(attrs={"autocomplete": "email"}))
    bio = forms.CharField(required=False, widget=forms.Textarea(attrs={"rows": 6}))
    birth_date = forms.DateField(widget=forms.DateInput(attrs={"type": "date"}))
    favourite = forms.ChoiceField(
        choices=[("django", "Django"), ("python", "Python")],
        widget=forms.RadioSelect,
    )
    avatar = forms.ImageField(required=False)
sections.note: `ImageField` needs Pillow installed. A `ModelChoiceField` queryset is evaluated when the form is rendered, so keep it small or filter it per user.

sections.title: What is_valid() actually does
sections.body:
This sequence explains most “why is my error not showing?” questions:

1. For each field, `Field.clean(value)` runs `to_python()`, `validate()` and `run_validators()`.
2. `Form._clean_fields()` stores successful values in `cleaned_data` and collects `ValidationError`s per field.
3. `Form.clean()` runs your cross-field checks on the cleaned values.
4. For a `ModelForm`, `_post_clean()` calls `instance.full_clean(exclude=...)` to apply model validation.
5. `is_valid()` returns `not self.errors` and caches the result. Calling `is_valid()` twice does not re-run validation.

If a field fails in step 1, its value is not in `cleaned_data` when `clean()` runs. Guard with `.get()` or let the field error stand.
sections.note: `add_error(field, error)` removes that field from `cleaned_data`. That is deliberate: invalid data should not look cleaned.

sections.title: Field validation: clean_<field>, clean and add_error
sections.body:
Use `clean_<fieldname>()` for one field. It receives the already-converted value and must return the value to keep. Use `clean()` for rules that involve several fields. Use `self.add_error("field", "message")` to attach an error to a specific field; `raise ValidationError` inside `clean()` becomes a non-field error.

Validators are reusable functions; `clean_<field>()` is form-specific. Prefer a validator when the same rule protects multiple forms or models.
sections.note: Do not raise `ValidationError` for a field error from `clean()` without a dict; it becomes a non-field error and may not appear next to the input.

sections.title: ModelForm: the 80% case
sections.body:
`ModelForm` reads fields, labels, help text and validators from a model. Declare `fields` explicitly; `__all__` exposes every column, including ones you did not mean to let users edit. Use `exclude` only when the excluded list is short and stable.

`form.save(commit=False)` gives you an unsaved instance so you can set fields the form should not control (author, tenant, timestamps). Call `form.save_m2m()` if the model has many-to-many fields and you used `commit=False`.
sections.note: ModelForm validation is not a substitute for database constraints. It runs in Python and can be bypassed by bulk operations.

sections.title: Initial data, limited choices and disabled fields
sections.body:
`initial` prefills an unbound form. `instance` binds a `ModelForm` to an existing row for editing. They are different: use `initial` for a new object with suggested values, and `instance` when the row already exists.

To limit a choice field to the current user, set the queryset in `__init__`. To make a field visible but not editable, set `disabled = True`; Django ignores submitted changes and uses the initial value. For a field that should not appear at all, remove it from `fields` or from `self.fields`.

Dynamic fields are fine, but add them before validation runs and document why they exist.
sections.code:
class BookingForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Booking
        fields = ["room", "starts_at", "guests", "notes"]

    def __init__(self, *args, user=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.fields["room"].queryset = Room.objects.filter(
            owner=user, is_active=True
        )
        if self.instance.pk:
            self.fields["starts_at"].disabled = True

# new object with suggested values
form = BookingForm(initial={"guests": 2}, user=request.user)

# edit an existing object
form = BookingForm(instance=booking, user=request.user)

# add a field that is not on the model
self.fields["coupon"] = forms.CharField(required=False)
sections.note: If you filter a queryset by user, the view must pass the user explicitly. A form has no reliable access to the request unless you give it one.

sections.title: Widgets, CSS classes and manual rendering
sections.body:
A field validates; a widget renders. Use `forms.TextInput`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `CheckboxInput`, `RadioSelect`, `FileInput`, `DateInput` and so on. Pass `attrs` for class, placeholder, autocomplete and rows.

For a whole form, set classes in `__init__` so you do not repeat them on every field. Render fields manually when the design needs labels above inputs, help text and errors in specific places. `{{ form.as_p }}` is for prototypes.

sections.title: Formsets: many forms on one page
sections.body:
A formset is a collection of the same form. `formset_factory` is for plain forms; `modelformset_factory` is for multiple model rows; `inlineformset_factory` is for children of one parent (order → items).

The management form is hidden bookkeeping. Render `{{ formset.management_form }}` inside the `<form>` or Django cannot tell how many forms were submitted. Set `extra`, `can_delete=True` and `max_num` deliberately.
sections.note: “ManagementForm data is missing or has been tampered with” almost always means `{{ formset.management_form }}` is missing, outside the form, or the formset changed between GET and POST.

sections.title: Files: request.FILES and validation
sections.body:
File inputs require `enctype="multipart/form-data"`. Django puts uploaded files in `request.FILES`, not `request.POST`. A `FileField` in a bound form needs both: `UploadForm(request.POST, request.FILES)`.

Validate size, content type and extension before saving. Client-side checks are UX, not security. Store files outside the source tree, give them non-guessable names, and serve private files through a permission-checked view, not `MEDIA_URL`.

sections.title: If the form is not working
sections.body:
Work through this list before changing random code:

- Is the form **bound**? `Form()` on POST will always be invalid or empty.
- Is `request.FILES` passed for a file upload?
- Is the submit using `method="post"` and does the form include `{% csrf_token %}`?
- Are you rendering `field.errors` and `form.non_field_errors` anywhere?
- Does the field name in HTML match the field name in `forms.py`?
- Does `clean_<field>()` return a value? Returning `None` removes it from `cleaned_data`.
- Is a `ModelForm` missing a required model field that is not in `fields`?
- Are you redirecting after success, or re-rendering with the same POST data?
sections.note: Remove debugging prints before committing; use Django's logging or a debugger instead.

pitfalls: Passing `request.POST` but forgetting `request.FILES` for an upload form.
Using `Form()` instead of `Form(request.POST)` on POST and wondering why `cleaned_data` is empty.
Putting `{% csrf_token %}` outside the `<form>` or forgetting it entirely.
Using `fields = "__all__"` on a ModelForm and letting users edit `is_staff` or `author`.
Raising a plain `ValidationError` in `clean()` for a field-specific problem.
checklist: The form is bound with `request.POST` (and `request.FILES` when needed).
Every field has a visible error path in the template.
`{% csrf_token %}` is inside every POST form.
Uploads validate size and type server-side.

errors.cause: The field failed validation, so it was removed from cleaned_data. Reading it before checking is_valid() or without a guard raises KeyError.
errors.fix: Check form.is_valid() first and use cleaned_data.get("fieldname"). Render field.errors so the real validation message is visible.

errors.cause: The browser sent an empty value, the input name does not match the form field, or the field is not inside the submitted form.
errors.fix: Inspect the rendered HTML name attribute, confirm the input is inside the form, and check whether the value is actually sent in the POST body.

errors.cause: The POST form has no {% csrf_token %}, the token is outside the form, or the request is cross-origin without a trusted origin.
errors.fix: Add {% csrf_token %} inside the form. For a separate frontend, send the X-CSRFToken header and configure CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS.

errors.error: ManagementForm data is missing or has been tampered with
errors.cause: The formset management form was not rendered, was rendered outside the form, or the number of forms changed without updating it.
errors.fix: Render {{ formset.management_form }} inside the form. When adding forms with JavaScript, update TOTAL_FORMS and INITIAL_FORMS.

errors.error: Select a valid choice. That choice is not one of the available choices.
errors.cause: The submitted value is not in the field's choices, often because the queryset changed or the value is a string instead of a primary key.
errors.fix: Check the ChoiceField/ModelChoiceField queryset, the option value, and whether the related object still exists.

errors.error: Cannot assign ...: instance is not saved / save() prohibited to prevent data loss
errors.cause: A ModelForm with commit=False was saved before required fields were set, or an unsaved related object was assigned.
errors.fix: Set the missing fields before save(), save the related object first, or use commit=True when no post-processing is needed.

errors.error: The view didn't return an HttpResponse object
errors.cause: The POST branch called is_valid() and then returned None on the invalid path.
errors.fix: Return render(...) with the bound form after the POST branch, so invalid submissions get a response with errors.
